schema: §2.7 (v0.50) -- complete per-sentence segment disposition, superseding §21 R6's not_annotatable-only shape. `not_annotatable` (R6's original array, the only key run_scoring.load_not_annotatable() reads) is preserved for scoring and holds every NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING / NOT_ANNOTATABLE / EXCLUDED span. `dispositions` is the full per-sentence record §2.7 requires, covering ANNOTATED and AMBIGUOUS spans too, which `not_annotatable` deliberately excludes -- an AMBIGUOUS span is an open reviewer question, not a settled non-item, and including it in the scoring array would resolve it silently.

reconciliation.obligation_bearing_clauses: INDETERMINATE: 2, 3 or 4 pending the candidate-2 ruling
reconciliation.note: AMENDED 2026-09-17 (b) -- obligation_bearing_clauses was left as the integer 3 by this same day's §8.8.4 amendment, which SILENTLY ENCODED ONE OF THE THREE LIVE READINGS of candidate 2 (namely that it yields exactly one item). Corrected to an explicit indeterminate. See holdout/C14_076_INVESTIGATION.md §10.3: with candidate 1 excluded the segment stands at 2 (C14-01 + C14-02), and candidate 2 adds 0, 1 or 2 -- giving 2, 3 or 4. ONLY THE 4 BRANCH BREACHES §2's 1-3 BAND; 3 sits at the ceiling and is eligible by settled precedent (the v0.50 ruling: 'C11-094 and C17-021 are NOT §2 band violations -- both sit exactly at the 1-3 band's ceiling at 3'). §4's 'candidate 2 ALONE puts the segment at 4' is therefore CORRECTED: it holds only if BOTH of candidate 2's verbs are obligation-bearing, a premise §4 never stated. PREVIOUS NOTE FOLLOWS, left as written per the corrections-are-new-text discipline: AMENDED 2026-09-17 (guideline v0.56) -- CANDIDATE 1 IS RULED NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING under the new §8.8.4 (ABSORB complement: a burden absorbed, not a performance rendered). obligation_bearing_clauses 4 -> 3. THE SEGMENT STAYS ESCALATED_BAND_RISK AND ITS STATUS IS UNCHANGED: candidate 2 alone takes the segment to 4 over §2's 1-3 band (its two verbs carry DIFFERENT OBLIGORS and one item has one obligor slot), so candidate 1 was never what decided eligibility -- investigation §4's correction (1), restated here because ruling candidate 1 makes it tempting to read the band risk as reduced. It is not. items_annotated stays 2 against 3 obligation-bearing clauses; the gap is candidate 2, still AMBIGUOUS and owed its own §14.4 session on the §5/§5.1 both-ABSENT question. C14-01/C14-02 are NOT in question. PREVIOUS NOTE FOLLOWS, left as written per the corrections-are-new-text discipline: AMENDED 2026-09-05 -- see holdout/C14_076_INVESTIGATION.md. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE NOTE BELOW. (1) THE BAND RISK IS NOT CONJUNCTIVE. Candidate 2 carries two verbs with DIFFERENT OBLIGORS (the payee adds VAT to its invoice; the payer pays it), and one item has one obligor slot, so it cannot be one item however section 4.3 is read. CANDIDATE 2 ALONE puts the segment at 4 and over section 2's 1-3 band, whatever candidate 1 turns out to be -- so candidate 2, not candidate 1, is what decides C14-01/C14-02's locked status, and it is the more urgent of the two escalations. (2) THE 'NEITHER ANNOTATOR RECORDED WHY' PREMISE IS FALSE -- the cold annotator disposed of both sentences with rules cited; candidate 1's disposition is sound, candidate 2's is contaminated by backwards reasoning from band eligibility. Both dispositions' full text and standing are in each reading below. Section 2.5 is also the wrong rule for candidate 1 (its trigger is unreviewable discretion); the governing family is section 8.8, in a cell holding 15 instances across 9 documents and no adjudicated precedent. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS, left as written per the corrections-are-new-text discipline: 4 obligation-bearing clauses vs 2 items_annotated. 2 clauses are AMBIGUOUS -- logged as a NEW TRACKED FINDING in CLAUDE.md (2026-09-04), deliberately NOT folded into SPLITTING_EXCLUSION_INVESTIGATION.md decisions 2-4 since it is a new discovery, not a known open question resurfacing. Checked directly rather than taken on citation: the precedent C02-04 cites ("C14-139's Q1") is forward guidance in a logged exclusion entry, never tested against a locked item -- neither candidate here matches either real precedent cleanly. Two real sub-questions scoped in CLAUDE.md: (a) does bare cost-allocation with no act-verb clear section 2.5's monitorable-stakes bar, (b) how does section 3.5.3 handle a fully agentless, partyless sentence with no worked precedent. IF BOTH CLAUSES ARE GENUINE, the segment totals 4 -- OVER section 2's 1-3 eligibility band, threatening C14-01/C14-02's own locked status. Scheduled as its own dedicated session, same tier as decisions 2-4 -- can wait alongside them, no urgency before batches 4-10 resume. C14-01/C14-02 are NOT themselves in question, only whether the segment is under-annotated.

dispositions.span_text: Each party will be solely responsible for any and all taxes imposed thereon, including, without limitation, all income taxes, sales taxes, goods and services taxes.
dispositions.reason: RULED 2026-09-17 (guideline v0.56, §14.4 §10 amendment session; full record in holdout/C14_076_INVESTIGATION.md §9). §8.8.4: in `be`/`remain responsible`/`liable for X` THE COMPLEMENT DECIDES, NOT THE CONSTRUCTION. This complement — 'any and all taxes imposed thereon' — names a BURDEN THE OBLIGOR MUST ABSORB, not a performance it must render or procure: the clause answers 'whose pocket?', not 'who must act?', and commands no conduct, which is §8.8.1's own removal test. THE PRIOR AMBIGUOUS REASON'S CITATION IS FALSIFIED AND IS THE REASON THE RULE IS ABOUT THE COMPLEMENT: it read C02-045 as 'almost identical "shall be solely responsible for" language', but C02-045 is 'responsible for THE TIMELY PAYMENT OF all such VAT and taxes TO THE APPLICABLE GOVERNMENTAL AUTHORITY' — an act, a payee and a standard, RENDER, locked as C02-04 action PAY. Near-identical construction, opposite complement. Measured over the 1,547-segment pool: 121 sentences, 106 segments; of 99 affirmative, RENDER 72 (17 docs) vs ABSORB 24 (11 docs). Discriminator 1 — the corpus writes 64 EXPLICIT pay/bear-the-cost duties across 17 documents, including all 9 of the 9 that also carry a cost-allocation instance, so allocation and payment are separately drafted. BAND CONSEQUENCE, STATED AGAINST INTEREST: this exclusion does NOT rescue the segment. Candidate 2 ALONE takes it to 4 obligation-bearing clauses (its two verbs have different obligors — investigation §4), so the segment stays ESCALATED_BAND_RISK and C14-01/C14-02's locked status is still undecided. ORIGINAL AMBIGUOUS REASON FOLLOWS, left as written per the corrections-are-new-text discipline: 'Each party will be solely responsible for any and all taxes imposed thereon ...' -- a plain 'each party'-subject MUST clause (same distributive-obligor shape as this segment's own C14-01/C14-02) with real precedent for annotatability: C02-045's locked item uses almost identical 'shall be solely responsible for' language. CONSEQUENTIAL: see this segment's reconciliation note -- if this and the next sentence are both genuine obligation-bearing clauses, the segment holds 4, over §2's 1-3 band.

readings.detail: obligor 'Each party' (distributive, matching C14-01/C14-02's own treatment), obligee ABSENT, action likely a taxonomy gap ('be responsible for' has no clean 34-verb match, nearest BEAR/WITHHOLD-adjacent), no rule excludes it.

readings.reading: Excluded by the cold annotator (CORRECTED 2026-09-05 — this reading previously asserted that neither annotator flagged the sentence)
readings.detail: CORRECTION: the previous text read 'Neither the gold drafter nor the independent cold annotator flagged this sentence ... but neither recorded why, so this retrofit cannot treat silence as a decision.' The second half is FALSE. The cold annotator disposed of this sentence explicitly and with rules cited: 'a copular "will be solely responsible" status assertion, which is section 8.8's measured "not an obligation clause at all" class; section 8.8.1 confirms the class turns on status-versus-conduct and not on negation placement ... NOT_ANNOTATABLE content (section 4.4).' This is a real reasoned exclusion and it is NOT contaminated -- it rests entirely on section 8.8/8.8.1 and cites no eligibility consequence. ONE LOAD-BEARING PART OF IT DOES NOT HOLD, checked rather than accepted: cold cites C04-163's 'shall not be responsible for payments' as 'the same construction affirmatively phrased', and it is not -- C04-163 differs on TWO axes at once (negative polarity AND an act-nominalisation complement, 'payments'), so it cannot settle this clause by citation. Measured: the affirmative + bare-burden cell has NO adjudicated instance anywhere in the gold set and holds 15 instances across 9 documents, so this is section 10 amendment territory under section 14.4's repeated-uncertainty rule, not a per-item call. Source: holdout/cold/17_C14-076.json's segment_notes; audited across all 22 retrofitted segments by holdout/band_risk/cold_dispositions.py

readings.detail: §3.5.3 agentless-passive treatment: obligor ABSENT (no agent stated), obligee ABSENT (no party named at all), underspecified=true. No rule excludes it as written. AMENDED 2026-09-05, checked against section 3.5.3's actual rule text rather than its worked cases: the rule ANTICIPATES this shape in terms -- 'Where no party is named at all, or more than one candidate is equally available, obligee = ABSENT' -- so field assignment is decidable by citation and is NOT the open question. The genuinely novel part is downstream: NO locked item among the 32 has BOTH slots ABSENT (the only two obligor-ABSENT items, C04-03 and C14-05, each carry an in-span obligee), so under section 5's 'ABSENT matches ABSENT' this would be the first item where two of eight scored clauses pass on a vacuous match -- a section 5/5.1 question, never asked. SPLITTING: the two verbs have DIFFERENT OBLIGORS (the payee adds VAT to its invoice; the payer pays it) and one item has one obligor slot, so this is TWO clauses independent of section 4.3's judgment call. Measured recurrence: 62 fully-partyless agentless performance passives (3.1% of modal sentences) across the 10 registry-backed documents.

readings.reading: Excluded by the cold annotator (CORRECTED 2026-09-05 — this reading previously asserted that neither annotator flagged the sentence)
readings.detail: CORRECTION: the previous text read 'Same as the preceding sentence: neither annotator flagged it, but neither recorded a reason.' FALSE. The cold annotator disposed of this sentence at length AND wrote out the competing section 3.5.3 reading in full, including obligor ABSENT / obligee ABSENT, the two-verb split, and 'if applicable' as a conditions entry. BUT THIS DISPOSITION IS CONTAMINATED AND MUST NOT BE RELIED ON: cold's second stated ground is 'admitting it would take the segment to 3-4 obligation-bearing clauses, pressing section 2's 1-3 band for no gain' -- reasoning backwards from the eligibility outcome, which is exactly what C14-139's process fix forbids ('eligibility is decided before content is adjudicated'). Cold's first ground (a tax-treatment rule rather than a commanded act) survives; its second does not. Source: holdout/cold/17_C14-076.json's segment_notes; audited across all 22 retrofitted segments by holdout/band_risk/cold_dispositions.py
